phases.name: Launchpad
phases.goal: Set the baseline, toolchain and career target: AI Cloud / GenAI Platform Engineering.

phases.name: Foundations + Cloud Core
phases.goal: Build Python/data foundations while starting cloud, Linux, networking and production habits early—not at the end.

phases.name: Core SWE + Cloud Engineering
phases.short: OS, DBMS, networks, distributed systems, AWS
phases.goal: Turn MERN experience into deep software engineering and cloud architecture capability; ship PairCraft with production evidence.

phases.name: GenAI Engineering + Retrieval
phases.short: RAG, evals, observability, AI platform basics
phases.goal: Build AtlasAI and learn retrieval, evaluation, security, model routing and cloud deployment patterns.

phases.name: ML + Deep Learning + Inference
phases.goal: Understand model internals and inference economics well enough to make production trade-offs.

phases.name: Agents + AI Reliability
phases.goal: Build reliable agentic systems with bounded autonomy, security and measurable quality.

phases.name: AI Cloud Platform + MLOps
phases.goal: Become an AI-cloud engineer: deploy, scale, secure, observe and optimize AI workloads.

phases.name: Interview + International Conversion
phases.goal: Convert the technical profile into strong domestic and international interviews/offers.

phases.name: Final Readiness + Year-2 Strategy
phases.goal: Polish evidence, define year-2 specialization and execute the job/relocation strategy.

These recall tasks DO count toward progress; the side-track modules do not. Existing W2–W13 Day-6 MERN revision sessions are kept.

decisions.title: One timeline: 52 weeks
decisions.text: Google roadmap and Blueprint are 12-month plans; career-roadmap-v4 and 1cr are 4-year career plans; the reference runs ~24 months. The OS schedules the first 12 months (learning + first conversions). Years 2–4 (PM bridge, specialization lanes, ₹1 Cr, Germany) live in Horizon.

decisions.title: DSA in Python
decisions.text: Google roadmap says C++, career-v4 says JavaScript, the reference says Python. Python wins: it doubles as AI-track practice, all owned AI courses use it, and it removes a third language. C++ is only worth it for C++-specific Google reqs — revisit in Horizon if a target JD demands it.

decisions.title: DSA volume = 175 problems × 2 passes
decisions.text: Google (350–450) and Blueprint (350–400) count solves; the reference argues 120–150 deeply + a cold second pass. NeetCode 150 + 25 India staples, each re-solved cold 2–4 weeks later ≈ 350 solve-events, plus timed sets and 15+ mocks.

decisions.title: DSA hours: 90 → 60 min/day
decisions.text: Blueprint Sheet 01 wants 21 h/week of DSA; Google wants 1 h 45/day; the reference 45–60 min/day. Compromise: 90 min in P1–P2, 75 in P3, 60 in P4–P6, then timed sessions/mocks in P7.

decisions.title: Projects consolidated to 3 flagships + capstone + 8 supporting
decisions.text: Sources list ~25 projects. ScaleQueue lives inside PairCraft (queue/workers/DLQ); SearchForge lives inside AtlasAI (BM25 + IR metrics); Clinical Notes + meeting-to-CRM merged into one mini project; startup/Shopify ideas kept in Horizon.

decisions.title: Certs are secondary to portfolio
decisions.text: The reference marks CCP/AI Practitioner as resume-filler and confirms AWS ML Specialty was retired on 31 Mar 2026 (career-v4 still recommends it — removed). Scheduled: GitHub Actions (free, W16) and AWS ML Engineer Associate (W44–W47, optional). CKA/SAA/AIGP → Horizon.

decisions.title: TypeScript migration removed as a task
decisions.text: career-v4 schedules a TS migration; the Blueprint states TS is already in the current stack. PairCraft is built in TypeScript end-to-end, which exercises it without a separate migration week.

decisions.title: Frontend track not scheduled
decisions.text: The Google curriculum lists frontend as a secondary track. As a MERN developer this is assumed; every project ships a real React UI, which is the practice.

decisions.title: Web3 track skipped
decisions.text: 100xSchool’s Web3 track is optional in career-v4 and absent from every other source; it would be an unrelated technology for this target.

decisions.title: Freelancing not scheduled
decisions.text: 1cr_roadmap suggests MERN freelancing from month 6. At 5 h/day it cannot fit without cutting DSA or projects; listed in Horizon as an income lever once the first switch lands.

decisions.title: MERN revision and DevOps go into the main path; cybersecurity and blockchain go into Side Tracks
decisions.text: Per your request. MERN and DevOps are directly on the target profile (every flagship ships a React UI and must run in production), so they are scheduled on Day 6, the lightest weekday, to keep every day near 5 hours. Cybersecurity and blockchain are useful but not on the critical path, so they live as self-paced side tracks that never displace DSA or a flagship milestone.

never_skip: DSA daily slot (even 30 min: one re-solve). Interview skill decays fastest and is the gate for every loop.
The current flagship’s milestone for the week — shipped evidence is what unlocks roles.
Phase gate assessments — they are the anti-checkbox-theater mechanism.
Weekly review notes — 10 minutes keeps the streak of reflection alive.
compress: Theory blocks (OS/DBMS/CN, math intuition): watch at 1.5×, do the “What you should know” questions only, skip the second resource.
Course videos: skip sections you can already answer cold; do the project of the week, not every lecture.
System-design cases: 1 case/week instead of 2; write the delta, skip re-watching.
Career block: batch LinkedIn/network tasks into one 60-minute session per week.
postpone: Nice-to-know tasks (🟢) — remove them from the week entirely and continue.
Optional certs (AWS AI Practitioner, AWS MLE-A) — move to Horizon without guilt.
Intermediate projects (gateway, risk model, MCP suite) — cut scope to their first two milestones.
OSS contribution — one PR is enough; later is fine.
skip_temporarily: Framework tours (W40 AutoGen/ADK/Strands) — build in one framework well instead of three.
Paper reading and newsletters — zero cost to pause.
Second backup resource on any topic — one spine per topic.
catch_up: Step 1 — Do not rewind. Open Today and complete the first unfinished day as written; do not try to “make up” missed days.
Step 2 — Run a 2-day triage: for each missed day, do only its 🔴 MUST KNOW tasks and its DSA problems (cap 5 h/day).
Step 3 — Cut the current week to must-know + the flagship milestone. Mark 🟡 as skipped in your weekly notes.
Step 4 — Re-run the last mastery checkpoint aloud; if ≥4/5 hold, continue; if not, spend one day on the “fail → revisit” items of the last phase gate.
Step 5 — Return to the normal schedule when: DSA slot done 3 days in a row AND the flagship milestone is back on track AND the weekly review is written.
rules: After 3+ missed days: do a 2-day triage, then continue.
After 2+ missed weeks: redo the last phase gate first (it takes one day), then continue from the first unfinished day.
After 1+ missed month: re-run the W1 diagnostic (10 problems cold) and the last two mastery checkpoints; keep Day 7 as a rest day for the first two weeks back.
Six or more hours a day burns out in 6–8 weeks (career-trajectory-playbook). Never “catch up” by doubling hours.

certifications.name: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate
certifications.why: Best first major cloud credential for this plan. It validates AWS architectural knowledge; use the exam as a structured milestone after hands-on VPC/IAM/EC2/S3/RDS/LB work.

certifications.name: HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (004)
certifications.why: Useful proof of infrastructure-as-code fundamentals after you have already provisioned real environments. Do not take it before using Terraform in a project.

certifications.name: Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA)
certifications.why: High-signal, hands-on, vendor-neutral Kubernetes credential. Schedule only after you can deploy, debug, network, secure and scale a real workload on Kubernetes.

certifications.name: AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer – Associate
certifications.why: Strong match for AI-cloud/ML platform work. AWS is updating MLA-C02 in 2026, adding broader GenAI/agent/foundation-model coverage; use the currently available exam guide when booking.

certifications.name: GitHub Actions Certification
certifications.why: Legitimate GitHub credential, but lower priority than AWS/CKA/Terraform. Earn it only if you want external validation for CI/CD.

certifications.name: AWS Certified AI Practitioner
certifications.why: Foundational AI credential. Useful for non-technical AI literacy, but redundant once you can implement and deploy production AI systems.

certifications.name: GCP Professional Machine Learning Engineer
certifications.why: Excellent certification, but Google recommends 3+ years industry experience including 1+ year designing/managing GCP solutions. Earn after real GCP experience, not during this first-year sprint.

certifications.name: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional
certifications.why: Advanced architecture signal; much more valuable after meaningful production AWS experience. The exam is being updated to SAP-C03 in late 2026.

certifications.name: AWS Security – Specialty
certifications.why: Strong credential for cloud security, but AWS positions it for experienced practitioners. Do not divert first-year effort from core AI-cloud skills.

certifications.name: Removed from plan: AWS ML Specialty
certifications.why: Do not follow old roadmap references to the retired ML Specialty; use AWS Machine Learning Engineer – Associate instead.

horizon.title: Months 13–18 — First switch + specialization fork
horizon.text: Take the strongest offer as the platform (Blueprint Branch B is normal). Keep DSA at 3–4 h/week. Pick ONE lane from the reference Step 8: LLMOps deep, Forward-Deployed Engineer, Indic NLP, CV, Safety, or Applied Science. Certs: CKA, then AWS SAA if a filter needs it.

horizon.title: Months 18–24 — Seniority layer
horizon.text: Reference Step 9: DDIA-level distributed design, multi-tenant AI platform architecture, RFCs/ADRs, one public talk or essay (StaffEng). Google roadmap “switch review” every 12 months; negotiate every offer with market bands in hand.

horizon.title: Years 2–3 — AI Platform / Agentic senior track
horizon.text: career-roadmap-v4 Phase 2–3: LLMOps, AI system architecture, technical leadership, GenAI in Production course (buy at month 18+), AWS SAP, GCP MLE. Project bank: AgriSense, FactoryMind, HireIQ, the 6 Shopify apps — pick by pull and revenue potential.

horizon.title: Years 3–4 — Technical AI PM bridge (optional)
horizon.text: career-roadmap-v4 Phase 4 + reference AI PM section: PRDs, eval-driven product thinking, POPM → PMP, Reforge. Only if the pull is real; infra as a skill layer, not an identity.

horizon.title: Income levers (1cr_roadmap, career-trajectory-playbook)
horizon.text: Switch every 18–24 months for 40–60% jumps; cap expenses; invest savings from month 1; MERN freelancing (Toptal/Contra) once the first switch lands; AI consulting from year 3; remote USD roles in year 4.

horizon.title: Germany / EU (certification report, reference CI-4, Working Abroad)
horizon.text: Blue Card or the no-degree IT-specialist route (3 yrs experience + recognized certs + employer reference). Start A2–B1 German 15 min/day from month 12. Re-verify thresholds on make-it-in-germany.com.

horizon.title: Communication muscle (career-trajectory-playbook)
horizon.text: Keep the three weekly habits: explain one technical thing to a non-technical person; force Context → Approach → Trade-offs → Result; practice the disagreement script. Negotiate something small every month.

horizon.title: Staying current (reference CI-5)
horizon.text: Two newsletters max (Latent Space + one more); follow builders who publish measurements; one paper/month; quarterly 15-minute self-audit of this roadmap.

sideTracks.name: JavaScript & MERN Refresher
sideTracks.note: The one side track that IS wired into the main path: it exists because MERN — especially JavaScript — is your current stack and it keeps fading. Do the modules here in order during Day 7 spare time (or 2–3 evenings a week for the first 8 weeks); the weekly 20–25 min recall tasks on Day 7 of W2–W52 (tagged [ADDED SUPPORTING TOPIC]) keep it alive and DO count toward roadmap progress. Rule: never read without typing — every module ends with something you built from memory.

modules.title: JS mental model: values, types, coercion, scope, hoisting
modules.learn: Primitives vs objects (copy vs reference), typeof/instanceof quirks, == vs === and the ToPrimitive/ToNumber coercion rules, truthy/falsy, NaN, hoisting of var/function vs TDZ for let/const, block vs function scope, execution context + creation phase, the global object, strict mode.
modules.do: Write coercion.js with 20 expressions ([] + {}, [] == ![], '5' - 2, null >= 0 …) — predict, run, explain each in one line. Then write a 10-snippet hoisting/TDZ quiz for yourself and pass it cold the next day.
check: Predict 18/20 coercion outputs and explain the rule behind each
Explain hoisting vs TDZ with a runnable example of each
Draw the creation vs execution phase of an execution context from memory

modules.title: Functions deep-dive: closures, this, call/apply/bind, HOFs
modules.learn: Lexical scope + closures (why loops with var break), the 4 rules of `this` (default, implicit, explicit, new) + arrow functions’ lexical this, call/apply/bind, IIFE, currying, partial application, higher-order functions, pure functions, the module pattern.
modules.do: Implement from memory: once, memoize (with Map cache key), debounce (leading/trailing), throttle, curry(fn), compose/pipe, a counter factory, and your own Function.prototype.myBind. Write a test file that proves each.
check: Write debounce + throttle + curry cold in ≤15 min with tests passing
State the 4 `this` rules and predict `this` in 8 snippets (method, extracted method, arrow in method, setTimeout callback…)
Explain a closure with the var-in-loop bug and the two fixes (let, IIFE)

modules.title: Objects, prototypes, classes, iterators & generators
modules.learn: Prototype chain lookup, __proto__ vs prototype, Object.create, constructor functions vs ES6 classes (fields, #private, static, getters/setters, super), inheritance vs composition/mixins, property descriptors, Object.freeze, Symbol, Symbol.iterator, generators, for…of vs for…in, getters and Proxy basics.
modules.do: Build the same Animal → Dog hierarchy three ways (prototype chain by hand, constructor+prototype, class) and prove they behave identically. Implement a Range class that is iterable with a generator, and a tiny observable store using Proxy.
check: Draw the prototype chain for a class instance including Function and Object
Explain how `class` desugars to prototypes
Write an iterable with a generator without notes

modules.title: Async JavaScript: event loop, promises, async/await
modules.learn: Call stack, Web APIs, macrotask (task) vs microtask queues, rendering steps, promise states and chaining, error propagation (why a missing return breaks a chain), Promise.all/allSettled/race/any, async/await as promise sugar, sequential vs parallel awaits, unhandled rejections, AbortController, event emitters, timers.
modules.do: Implement MyPromise (then/catch/finally, chaining, microtask scheduling with queueMicrotask) and pass a 15-case test. Implement Promise.all, allSettled, race and a promisify helper from memory. Then take 25 ordering snippets (setTimeout / Promise / queueMicrotask / async function mixes), predict output, run in Loupe / Node.
check: Predict 12/12 event-loop ordering snippets correctly
Implement Promise.all + allSettled cold in ≤10 min
Explain why `await` in a for-loop is sequential and how to parallelize safely with a concurrency limit

modules.title: Modern JS toolkit: ES6+, collections, immutability, modules, errors
modules.learn: Destructuring, spread/rest, default params, template literals, optional chaining/nullish coalescing, array methods (map/filter/reduce/flatMap/find/some/every/sort comparator pitfalls), Map/Set/WeakMap/WeakRef, structuredClone vs JSON deep copy, immutability patterns, Date/Intl basics, RegExp basics, ESM vs CommonJS (loading, live bindings, top-level await), Error subclasses and cause, try/catch/finally.
modules.do: Implement deepClone (handles cycles via WeakMap), flatten(arr, depth), groupBy, chunk, uniqueBy, and a LRU cache with Map. Convert one small CJS project to ESM and document the 5 things that broke.
check: Write deepClone with cycle handling cold
Explain ESM vs CJS: hoisting of imports, live bindings, `this`, default interop
Use reduce to build an index/groupBy without looking up the signature

modules.title: Browser platform: DOM, events, fetch, storage, rendering
modules.learn: DOM traversal/manipulation, event flow (capture → target → bubble), delegation, passive listeners, custom events, fetch + streaming + AbortController, CORS (simple vs preflight), cookies vs localStorage vs IndexedDB, the rendering pipeline (style → layout → paint → composite), reflow vs repaint, requestAnimationFrame, IntersectionObserver, Web Workers, Core Web Vitals.
modules.do: Build a vanilla-JS todo app with event delegation, optimistic UI and fetch to a mock API — no framework. Add an infinite-scroll list with IntersectionObserver and measure layout thrash with DevTools Performance, then fix it.
check: Explain event delegation and implement it for a dynamic list
Explain a CORS preflight and which headers trigger it
Name what causes reflow vs repaint and one fix for each

modules.title: TypeScript essentials for MERN
modules.learn: Structural typing, interfaces vs type aliases, unions + narrowing + discriminated unions, generics with constraints, utility types (Partial/Required/Pick/Omit/Record/ReturnType/Awaited), keyof/typeof/indexed access, satisfies, unknown vs any, strict mode flags, typing Express handlers and React props/hooks, zod for runtime + static types.
modules.do: Type a small API client (fetchJson<T>, typed error union, Result type) with zero `any`; type a React form component with generic field config. Turn on strict and fix every error in one existing project.
check: Write a generic Result<T,E> + narrowing without notes
Explain when to use interface vs type, unknown vs any
Type a custom hook’s return tuple correctly

modules.title: Node.js internals: event loop phases, streams, modules, processes
modules.learn: Node event-loop phases (timers → pending → poll → check → close), process.nextTick vs setImmediate vs setTimeout(0), libuv thread pool, streams (readable/writable/transform, pipeline, backpressure), Buffers, fs/path, EventEmitter, child_process vs worker_threads vs cluster, environment/config, npm scripts, package.json exports, semver, lockfiles.
modules.do: Stream a 1 GB file through a gzip transform with pipeline() and observe memory. Write an EventEmitter-based job runner with graceful shutdown on SIGTERM. Prove the nextTick/setImmediate ordering with a script and explain it.
check: Draw Node’s event-loop phases and place nextTick/microtasks correctly
Explain backpressure and show it with pipeline()
Explain when to use worker_threads vs cluster vs child_process

modules.title: Express & API design done right
modules.learn: Middleware order and next(err), async error handling (express-async-errors or wrapper), routers and versioning, validation with zod, REST conventions (status codes, pagination, filtering, idempotency keys), auth middleware (JWT access/refresh, sessions + cookies), rate limiting, helmet/CORS, structured logging (pino), request IDs, health checks, layered structure (routes → controllers → services → repos).
modules.do: Build a reference API (users + posts) with the full layered structure, zod validation, central error handler, JWT auth with refresh rotation, rate limiting and supertest tests — fresh, from memory, in one sitting. Diff it against an old project and list what you would change there.
check: Explain middleware ordering and why error middleware needs 4 args
Implement access + refresh rotation and name 2 attacks it prevents
Produce a correct pagination + idempotent POST design in 5 min

modules.title: MongoDB & Mongoose: modelling, aggregation, indexes
modules.learn: Document modelling (embed vs reference, bounded arrays, bucket pattern), CRUD operators, aggregation pipeline ($match/$group/$lookup/$unwind/$project/$facet/$addFields), indexes (compound, ESR rule, covered queries, TTL, text), explain() and COLLSCAN vs IXSCAN, transactions, change streams, Mongoose schemas/validation/middleware/virtuals/populate/lean, connection handling and pooling.
modules.do: Model a blog with comments + tags three ways and argue the trade-offs. Write 10 aggregation queries against a sample dataset; use explain() to fix 2 slow ones with the right compound index. Add Mongoose pre-save hashing + a virtual + populate to one model.
check: Explain embed vs reference with a rule of thumb and 2 exceptions
Write $lookup + $group + $project cold and read its explain()
State the ESR rule and design a compound index for a given query

modules.title: React core: rendering model, state, effects, refs, forms
modules.learn: JSX → createElement, components as functions of props/state, render → commit phases, reconciliation and keys, state batching, immutability of state, controlled vs uncontrolled inputs, useEffect rules (deps, cleanup, sync-with-external-system), stale closures, useRef for values and DOM, lifting state, composition over inheritance, context and its re-render cost, error boundaries, Strict Mode double-invoke.
modules.do: Build a 300-line app (searchable, sortable, paginated table with a form) with zero libraries. Deliberately create a stale-closure bug and an infinite effect loop, then fix and explain both. Profile with React DevTools and remove one unnecessary re-render.
check: Explain render vs commit and what triggers a re-render
Fix a stale-closure and an effect dependency bug on sight
Explain why keys matter with a concrete reordering bug

modules.title: React advanced: performance, hooks, data fetching, routing, state libs
modules.learn: React.memo/useMemo/useCallback (when they help and when they hurt), custom hooks design, useReducer, context splitting, Suspense + lazy, error boundaries, TanStack Query (caching, invalidation, mutations, optimistic updates), Zustand vs Redux Toolkit vs context, React Router data APIs, forms with react-hook-form + zod, accessibility basics, Next.js App Router server vs client components.
modules.do: Refactor the module-11 app: extract 3 custom hooks, move server state to TanStack Query with optimistic updates, add code-split routes and an error boundary. Measure bundle size before/after.
check: Explain when useMemo is a net negative
Implement an optimistic mutation with rollback
Compare context vs Zustand vs Redux Toolkit for 3 concrete scenarios

modules.title: Full-stack integration: auth end-to-end, realtime, testing, deploy
modules.learn: Monorepo/project structure, env/config, auth flow end-to-end (cookie vs bearer, refresh, protected routes on the client), file uploads (multer → S3/presigned URLs), WebSockets/Socket.IO basics, CORS + proxies in dev, testing pyramid (Vitest, React Testing Library, supertest, Playwright), Dockerfile + compose for MERN, CI, deploy (Render/Railway/Vercel + Atlas), logging and health checks in prod.
modules.do: Ship a small full-stack app end-to-end in a weekend: login → protected dashboard → CRUD → realtime notifications, with 10 tests across the pyramid and a Dockerized deploy. Write a 1-page ‘how it works’ doc from memory.
check: Draw the end-to-end auth flow (client, API, DB, cookies) from memory
Explain the testing pyramid and what each layer catches
Deploy a MERN app with env secrets handled correctly

modules.title: Interview drill: output prediction, polyfills, machine coding
modules.learn: The standard JS interview bank: predict-the-output (event loop, this, hoisting, closures, coercion), polyfills (map/filter/reduce/bind/call/apply, Promise.all, debounce, deepClone, flatten, curry, EventEmitter, LRU), React machine-coding rounds (autocomplete, infinite scroll, modal, star rating, tabs), Node/DB design questions.
modules.do: Do 50 questions from the Lydia Hallie bank in 2 sittings; log every miss in mistakes.md with the rule you missed. Then write all 12 polyfills cold in one 60-min timed session. Do 2 React machine-coding tasks in 45 min each with a timer.
check: ≥45/50 on the question bank on a second cold pass
12 polyfills in ≤60 min with passing tests
Autocomplete with debounce + abort + keyboard nav in 45 min

modules.do: Review your AWS account: no root usage, MFA, least-privilege roles for each service, no public buckets, CloudTrail on. Write the checklist you used.

Explain the shared-responsibility model

modules.do: Run your W42 red-team suite against the capstone; add 5 new attack cases; document results.

modules.learn: CTF-style practice keeps the skill alive.

modules.title: Ethereum model
modules.learn: Accounts (EOA vs contract), transactions, gas, the EVM, state, events/logs, L2 rollups at intuition level, wallets and keys.
modules.do: Send a testnet transaction from a script; read its receipt and logs; estimate gas for a contract call.
check: Explain gas and why a transaction can fail after paying
EOA vs contract account in one minute

modules.title: Solidity basics
modules.learn: Types, storage vs memory, functions/modifiers, events, errors, inheritance, ERC-20/ERC-721 standards.
modules.do: CryptoZombies lessons 1–4; then write an ERC-20 token with OpenZeppelin and unit tests.
check: Explain storage vs memory cost
Token contract with 5 passing tests

modules.title: Contract dev workflow
modules.learn: Hardhat or Foundry: compile, test, local node, deploy scripts, verification, upgradeability caveats.
modules.do: Deploy your token + a simple escrow contract to a testnet with a scripted pipeline; verify on the explorer.
check: Reproducible deploy script
Escrow releases funds only on both signatures

modules.title: dApp frontend (your MERN edge)
modules.learn: Wallet connection, signing, reading/writing contracts from React with wagmi/viem or ethers, handling pending/failed transactions, indexing events.
modules.do: Mini project: a React dApp for your escrow contract with wallet connect, live balance, transaction status and an event feed; deploy on Vercel.
check: Wallet connect + one write transaction from the UI
Event feed updates without reload

modules.title: Smart-contract security
modules.learn: Reentrancy, integer/overflow history, access control, front-running/MEV, oracle manipulation, checks-effects-interactions, audits.
modules.do: Ethernaut levels 1–8; fix a deliberately reentrant contract; add a security section to your dApp README.
check: Explain reentrancy and CEI pattern
Ethernaut level 8 solved

careerBlueprint.title: AI Cloud Engineering → International Senior/Staff → MBA as a multiplier
careerBlueprint.northStar: Become a production-grade AI Cloud / GenAI Platform Engineer who can design, deploy, secure, observe and optimize AI systems at scale.
nonGoals: Learning every cloud equally in year 1
Using an MBA as a substitute for technical depth
skillPillars: Python + TypeScript, APIs, testing, Git, Linux, networking, OS, DBMS, distributed systems
AWS architecture, VPC, IAM, EC2/ECS/EKS, S3, RDS, Redis, queues, DNS, CDN, security, cost
LLM APIs, structured outputs, embeddings, RAG, evals, guardrails, agents, MCP, prompt/context engineering
Statistics, classical ML, PyTorch, transformers, fine-tuning, quantization, batching, GPU/VRAM, serving
Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD, registries, MLflow, observability, SLOs, rollback, FinOps
PairCraft, AtlasAI, Paper-to-Prod, benchmarks, postmortems, OSS PRs, technical writing
careerBlueprint.weeklyAllocation: Use the existing daily plan as the spine. Inside roughly 5 focused hours/day: 60–75m DSA, 2–2.5h primary engineering/AI-cloud task, 45–60m project/build, 20–30m interview/career. Cloud is a parallel track from W8 onward rather than a final-quarter add-on.
careerBlueprint.certLadder: SAA → Terraform Associate → CKA → AWS ML Engineer Associate. Add GitHub Actions only as a supporting credential. Defer GCP PMLE and AWS Solutions Architect Professional until you have the experience their official guidance expects.
careerBlueprint.proofRule: For every certification, require a matching artifact: architecture diagram, Terraform repo, Kubernetes deployment, benchmark, postmortem or production-style demo. A certificate without proof-of-work should not be counted as a milestone.
careerBlueprint.year2: Choose one specialization after real job feedback: AI platform/inference, cloud architecture, security/DevSecOps, or AI product/technical leadership. Add a top international MBA later only if it opens a role/network that your experience cannot unlock alone.
